text: dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth 是面向 DSH Web 的模型接入插件：它把支持 OAuth 的订阅账号注册为 LLM provider，并在 Settings 中提供订阅管理界面。已读入口列出 Kimi、Grok、Google Antigravity、GLM、Ark、MiMo 与 WorkBuddy 路由，并提供 Auto 路由；用户可在订阅设置中连接账号、查看模型和调整模型顺序，Auto 会按候选顺序尝试模型。适合希望通过已有订阅使用多家模型服务的 DSH 用户。插件不要求 API key；需要所选服务的账号授权，模型请求会发往对应服务端点。

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth connects subscription accounts to DSH Web as LLM providers. Its Settings page supports Kimi, Grok, Antigravity, GLM, Ark, MiMo, and WorkBuddy sign-in. Auto tries arranged models in order. No API key is required; requests go to provider services.
想用已有的 AI 订阅账号在 DSH 里调用模型，而不想单独配置 API key。
能不能在 DSH 设置里登录不同模型服务，并把它们的模型放进选择器？
Let me sign in to several providers and automatically try the next model when one is unavailable.
dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth 的功能「订阅模型接入」：将启用的订阅服务注册为 DSH LLM provider；用户可在 Settings 的 Subscriptions 页面连接账号，并在会话中选择其模型。
dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth 的功能「Auto 模型回退」：用户可使用 Auto 路由按排列顺序尝试候选模型；实现会在特定 provider 错误时继续尝试后续候选。
dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth 使用前须知：Kimi 登录使用 auth.kimi.com，模型列表与推理请求发往 api.kimi.com。（见 src/constants.ts:18-28）

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth：**Use the AI subscriptions you already pay for as LLM providers in DeepSeek Harness — no API key.**

Sign in once per provider from **Settings → Subscriptions** and that provider's models join the session model picker, with its plan quota shown live next to the connection. Tokens stay on your machine; every request streams through the provider's own API.

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth)
[](LICENSE)

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · Supported providers：| Provider | What you get | Sign-in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Kimi Code** | `kimi-for-coding`, `k3` (1M), `k3-256k` — read from the endpoint's own model list | OAuth device flow (show code, confirm in browser) |
| **Grok (X Premium)** | whatever the account's own model list reports (e.g. `grok-4.7`), **⚡ lightspeed** fast variant | Browser OAuth (auto-redirect) |
| **Google Antigravity** | Claude Sonnet/Opus, Gemini Flash, GPT-OSS, with reasoning tiers — read from the account's own list | Google account OAuth |
| **GLM (BigModel)** | whatever the coding host lists (e.g. `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.3-flash`) | ZCode browser sign-in (polled) |
| **Volcengine Ark** | the plan's own coding models | Volcengine SSO |
| **Xiaomi MiMo** | MiMo's own model list, with the app's two-model set as the fallback | Xiaomi account (QR / password) |
| **WorkBuddy (国内版)** | Hy, GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, MiniMax models | Browser OAuth (Tencent) |

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · Supported providers：Every provider also feeds the **`auto`** route, which spans them all: pick `auto` and the harness walks your enabled models in order until one answers.

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · Features：- **One sign-in per provider** — no API keys to find, paste, or rotate. The plugin runs the provider's own OAuth/device flow and keeps the token on disk (`~/.dsh/plugins/kimi-oauth/auth.json`, mode `0600`).
- **Live plan usage** — the Settings card and the composer chip show each account's remaining quota (Kimi's 5-hour / weekly windows + credit, Grok's weekly credit, Antigravity's Gemini + Claude buckets, GLM/Ark/MiMo/WorkBuddy credits), with a meter and reset time.
- **Model picker integration** — each provider's models appear in the session picker with context windows and reasoning tiers; hide or re-order them per provider.
- **Catalogs come from the provider, not from this build** — every route reads its own model list once and caches it as the provider's table, so a model released, renamed or retired server-side shows up (or disappears) without a plugin update. Signing in and the Settings **refresh models** action are what re-read it; browsing the picker never spends a request.
- **⚡ Fast / lightspeed variants** — for models that have one (e.g. Grok 4.7 → `grok-4.7-build-fast`), a bolt button beside the model selector switches to

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth
```

Then restart DeepSeek Harness and open **Settings → Subscriptions** (订阅).

To install a specific version, or straight from the repository:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth@0.10.2
dsh plugin --profile web add github:EricFL1998/dsh-subscription-oauth
```

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · How to use：1. **Open Settings → Subscriptions.** You see one card per provider; signed-in providers sort to the front, `auto` leads.
2. **Connect** a provider. A browser window (or a device code) starts the provider's own sign-in. Finish it there — the card updates by itself.
3. **Pick a model.** The provider's models now appear in the composer model picker, and the chip shows live usage.
4. **Expand a card** to manage accounts (set default, sign out, refresh token), toggle which models appear, re-order them, add a model id this build doesn't know yet, and see the credential file / endpoints.

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · How to use：> **Tip:** to use a different account on a provider, sign out first, then connect again — the browser sign-in follows whichever account the provider's page is signed in with.

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · What it registers：| Surface | What appears |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.llm` | the `kimi`, `grok`, `antigravity`, `glm`, `ark`, `mimo`, `workbuddy` and `auto` provider routes (models, reasoning, streaming) |
| Settings | a **Subscriptions** section: one card per provider |
| Model picker | each provider's own models, plus **`auto`** spanning them all |
| Composer chip | live plan usage for the provider in force |

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · Hiding a provider：To keep a provider's models out of the picker without uninstalling, drop it from the route list in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yml

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml：plugins:
  dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth:
    providers: [kimi, grok, antigravity, glm, ark, mimo, workbuddy]
```

Omit the ones you don't want. The list defaults to every implemented route.

dsh-plugin-subscription-oauth README · Security：- Credentials are stored locally at `~/.dsh/plugins/kimi-oauth/auth.json` (mode `0600`, written atomically), one section per provider.
- The plugin talks only to the providers' own hosts and OAuth endpoints — no telemetry, no third-party relay.
- Your subscriptions only; nothing is shared across machines.
